cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you say among people is being weighed as you say it.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: When something your people hold matters to you, do it with someone rather than explain it — let them watch the feeling in your hands, not in your words.
cells.core:
Where meaning is shared, you say the true thing at the size it can be heard. Someone repeats a story wrong, and you don't correct them flat; you tell it again the way it happened, and the telling carries the correction. Truth stays whole through the shape you give it, not through volume. People can hold more of what's real around you because you don't hand it to them all at once.

Next time you're passing on something that matters, do the thing rather than describe it. Whatever you feel about it, let someone see it in the doing, then let them take it from there. You won't be there for the part where they say it back wrong. That's what makes it theirs.
cells.sheetLine: You hand over clear meaning at the size it can be carried.
cells.verb: Weighing what gets said so clear meaning survives the passing on
cells.place: Where shared meaning and tradition are carried between people

cells.tense: You will be bracing for the moment the shared thing gets broken, and writing the repair before anyone has spoken.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Name the shared thing you most want to last, then give it the same small care every week — the call, the reading, the gathering — and hold that amount steady even when it feels thin.
cells.core:
You can feel where meaning is thinning in your group before anyone says so, and the repair starts running early. What gets said gets pre-corrected; the ritual gets shored up before it wobbles; you arrive with the answer and the room hasn't asked. The worry is real and it's moving faster than the people in it.

Steady beats early. Choose the shared thing you most want to last, and give it your same small attention weekly — the reading, the call, the ritual kept — and trust the repetition to carry what one big push would bruise. Some of it will drift while you're not guarding it, and you'll find out whether it needed guarding. Warmth that doesn't spike lasts longer. You can find out slowly.
cells.sheetLine: You'll be repairing the shared thing before anyone has spoken.
cells.verb: Weighing what gets said so clear meaning survives the passing on
cells.place: Where shared meaning and tradition are carried between people

cells.tense: You stood at the door of the shared thing, and something in you is still standing there.
cells.act: hold space for what someone feels without fixing it
cells.ask: Ask someone what a shared thing means to them, and when they answer, don't smooth or correct — stay quiet and let their answer be the whole of what happens next.
cells.core:
The room where meaning gets carried is one you know, and you're not fully in it. Words get weighed before they leave and then don't leave; you hold the clear version privately, and what gets passed around you is thinner than what you carry. People aren't getting the part of you that knows how to say the true thing gently.

You don't mend this by saying more. Sit with someone and ask what a shared thing means to them, then don't reach to sharpen, correct or fill. Their answer can stand without your hands on it. You'll feel the pull to improve it, and the pull is the habit, not the truth. Connection returns through being with someone's meaning rather than managing it. Stay long enough to hear what they actually hold.
cells.sheetLine: You weigh the words, then don't hand them over.
cells.verb: Weighing what gets said so clear meaning survives the passing on
cells.place: Where shared meaning and tradition are carried between people

cells.tense: You are shaping how something is said among people, and writing it off as the way the room happens to talk.
cells.act: make a ritual of the shared thing
cells.ask: Take a shared practice your people already keep and hold it on purpose this week — do it once, deliberately, and notice the words you reach for, the way you open it, the way you bring others in.
cells.core:
You set the phrasing your group ends up using. The way something gets said around you, the shape a story takes when you tell it — that's you shaping meaning, and from the inside it feels like nothing, like just talking. If someone asked how a practice started in your circle, you'd point at circumstance. You'd be pointing at yourself.

Take a shared practice your people already keep and hold it deliberately for a week. Do it once, on purpose, and notice the part that is yours — the words you reach for, the way you open it, the way you bring others in. You lose the cover of it being automatic, and you find what was you the whole time. It'll fit better than the version where it wasn't.
cells.sheetLine: The way the room talks is you, filed under habit.
cells.verb: Weighing what gets said so clear meaning survives the passing on
cells.place: Where shared meaning and tradition are carried between people

attempts.check: The draft says the person is the one keeping a shared meaning alive for a group; the record only supports that they calibrate and hold clarity with care where meaning is shared, not that anyone is leaning on them for it. A reader could reasonably say the group is not theirs to tend, or that the holding is mutual and no one is carrying anyone. The asks are still useful if the read is wrong because each one is a small, observable act in shared meaning that teaches something whether or not the excess or absence is real. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you are the one who holds it' — cut.
